## Summary

Sony Interactive Entertainment is the PlayStation company: Sony and Sony Music Entertainment Japan set it up in Tokyo in 1993 as Sony Computer Entertainment, it took its present name on 1 April 2016 when it merged with Sony Network Entertainment International, it is now headquartered in San Mateo, California, and its parent is Sony Group Corporation [2]. The IEEE registry lists 43 MA-L blocks to "Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc." at a Minato-ku, Tokyo address [1]. A MAC in one of these blocks is most likely a PlayStation console or other PlayStation product [2].

The PlayStation 5 uses Sony's own J20H100 wireless module, certified under FCC ID AK8M19DFR1, with antennas for Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.1 and a 2x2 802.11a/b/g/n/ac/ax radio on 2.4 and 5 GHz; a teardown-based analysis believes the chip inside is NXP's 88W9000S, a 2x2 dual-band WLAN and Bluetooth 5.1 combo [3]. TechInsights' PlayStation 5 Pro teardown names a MediaTek MT3605AEN supporting Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 5.1 [4].

In April 2011 an intrusion into the PlayStation Network compromised personal details from about 77 million accounts, and Sony took the network down for about 24 days [5]. Whether PlayStation consoles randomise their Wi-Fi address is not documented by any source consulted, so randomization is unknown. The FCC ID databases (fccid.io, fcc.report) refused automated access from this session, so the grantee code is given only as it appears in the cited module certification.
